instructions: Melt 1 tsp of the ghee in a 3-quart pot over medium-low heat. Add the moong dal and stir for 5 minutes, until it smells toasty and turns pale gold. Don't let it brown.
Transfer the dal to a bowl, add the rice, and rinse both in cold water, changing the water until it runs clear. Drain well.
Return the rice and dal to the pot. Add 5 cups water and the salt and bring to a boil over high heat. Turn the heat to low and set the lid on slightly open.
Cook for 25 minutes, stirring from the bottom every 5 minutes, until the rice and dal are very soft and falling apart. If it gets thick before that, stir in 1/2 cup hot water.
Meanwhile, peel and finely chop the ginger. Crush the peppercorns coarsely with a mortar and pestle or under the bottom of a pan.
Melt the remaining 1/4 cup ghee in a small skillet over medium heat. Add the cumin and the crushed pepper. After about 20 seconds they will sizzle and smell toasty.
Turn the heat to low and add the ginger. Cook for 30 seconds, then add the curry leaves and cook until they are crisp, about 30 seconds. Stand back a little. They will spatter.
Add the asafoetida and take the skillet off the heat.
Pour the ghee mixture into the pongal and stir well. Cover and leave it for 2 minutes. The pongal should be soft and loose. Stir in a splash of hot water if it is stiff.
Taste it. If it's flat, add a pinch more salt.
Serve hot with coconut chutney or sambar.
method_notes: Hebbar's Kitchen (5 from 485) is the lead for the proportions: equal rice and moong dal, about 7 parts water, a pepper, cumin, ginger and curry leaf tempering in ghee. It cooks in a pressure cooker, so the pot method here follows Swasthi's Recipes (4.99 from 296): dry-roast the dal, simmer until mushy, loosen with hot water. The lead uses 1/2 cup ghee for 3 servings, far more than Swasthi's 2 to 3 tablespoons, so this uses 1/4 cup for 4. Cashews (in both sources) and green chilies are left out to keep it nut-free and mild.
